reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 (1989 amendment) argument-2 of FUNCTION ANNUITY must be an integer argument (§1989:A.2.2 AR4: an arithmetic expression that always results in an integer value; an integer item, integer literal or integer function, never a numeric function per §1989:A.2.3 GR2), which the compiler must refuse when it is not, and its positive value is a permissible-value constraint whose breach leaves the result undefined (§1989:A.2.2 p3); for a legal argument-2 the function returns argument-1/(1-(1+argument-1)**(-argument-2)), or 1/argument-2 when argument-1 is zero.

reader.notes: The type half of AR3 (integer) is decided at compile time by the edition-independent IntegerViolation screen over the Verified row Schema(['n','i']); every non-integer shape probed is refused with COBOL1627 citing §1989:A.2.2 AR4 at 85. The positive half is a value constraint, undefined on breach at 1985 (§1989:A.2.2 p3), and the run time terminates the run unit through ExceptionState.ArgumentError's IsCobol85 arm. Minor and outside this rule: the COMP-1 refusal at --std 85 still names ISO §2023:14.6.8.3 in its body (the floating arm of NonIntegralItemReason is not edition-designated).
reader.at-2023: the same compile-time refusals (citing §2023:15.3 AR6); ANNUITY(0 0) returns 0 with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking off

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/w20262131/coderead/out/refute-1985-c02/src (runs/ beside it). Legal argument-2 forms the reader did not try all ran correctly: integer functions whose type depends on their arguments (intfn.cob ANNUITY(0 FUNCTION SUM(A B)) = 0.142857142 = 1/7; legal2.cob ANNUITY(0 BN) with BN PIC S9(4) BINARY = 0.2, ANNUITY(0 ZERO + 4) = 0.25, ZERO being an arithmetic-expression term at 85 per §1985:VI.6.2.1), wide values (big.cob ANNUITY(0 C) with C = 999999999999999998 -> 0 at 17 places; ANNUITY(0.000000001 1) = 1.000000001, RV2), and an undecided expression FUNCTION ORD(X) / 2 (c_annord.cob, 1/33). Refusal half: argument-2 FUNCTION MIN(A 2.5) (r_annmix.cob, a numeric function by its mixed arguments) and (FUNCTION REM(7 4)) in parentheses (p_ann.cob) are both refused COBOL1627 citing §1989:A.2.3. Class c: FUNCTION ABS/SIGN/BYTE-LENGTH (2002) and BINARY-LONG (2002) refused at 85 (c_abs, c_sign, c_blen, c_binlong). Readings considered and not decisive: (1) the literal 2.0 is accepted though §1985:III.2 Integer (1) excludes a literal with digits right of the decimal point, but §1989:A.2.2 AR4 defines the integer argument as an arithmetic expression that always results in an integer value, which 2.0 is; reading III.2 as exclusive would bar N + 1 too, which AR4 plainly admits. (2) An expression whose term is a numeric function (FUNCTION SQRT(A) * 1, p_mul1.cob) is accepted and checked at run time (c_sqrtv.cob terminates naming 2.732...), as D-INTEGER-ARGUMENT-SCREEN determines; §1985:I.1.6 makes a breach's result undefined, so this is not a conformance failure. cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.6.3 AR3 'Argument-2 must be a positive integer'; OK §1989:A.2.2 AR4 'An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified'; OK §1989:A.2.3 GR2 'A numeric function may not be referenced where an integer operand is required'; OK §1989:A.2.2 p3 'then the result of such a reference is undefined'; OK §1985:VI.6.2.1 'the figurative constant ZERO (ZEROS, ZEROES)'; OK §1985:I.1.6 'The results of violating the formats or rules of Standard COBOL are undefined'.
